name: Public authority records (branch root) — REFUSED
one_line: REFUSED. The roster hint defines this row as a document issued by or addressed to a public body that carries an authority and a record type but no more specific governmental sub-domain — which is not an organizational situation but the ABSENCE of one, sitting on top of thirty named government siblings. Its detection signals are the government schema's own authority-side signals, its dimension order is the schema's empty order, and its privacy posture is the schema's potentially_sensitive default, so it fails all three legs of the node test. The coverage is already held twice over: the government schema's own default template accepts any file that legitimately activates the schema without a sibling situation firing, and 00's residual homes — Independent Records, Protected Records, Reading Inbox, Review Later, Unsupported or Encrypted — hold the standalone official document that never reaches a group. Placeholder row (J-IND / PR-6): it writes NO field rows, because the government schema declares none.
refuse_reason: Fails the node test on all three legs of CONNECTION.md's rule that a template row exists only when its detection signals, recommended dimensions, or privacy rules differ from its schema's default template. (1) DETECTION SIGNALS — identical to the schema's. The government anchor already enumerates authority-side signals for every one of its thirteen work types (legislature packets, rulemaking dockets, public-body governance cycles, funder-side grant files, buyer-side procurement, deciding-side permit and enforcement cases, records-holder-side disclosure work, statistical collection cycles, election operations, citizen casework, public education and cultural administration, intergovernmental programmes). A file carrying authority-side evidence but no sibling-specific structure activates the `government` schema and lands on that default template; there is no further signal for this row to contribute. The only signal that would belong to this row and not to the schema is "a public body owns it AND no sibling fired", which is an absence conjoined with an organisation-type token that the schema itself lists first among its never_alone items: "a government department, regulator, municipality, legislature, court, public school, archive, museum, or official-looking seal alone; the entity may be issuer, counterparty, subject, employer, cited authority, research venue, or service provider". A row whose entire distinguishing evidence is never-alone can never clear activation. (2) DIMENSIONS — identical, and empty on both sides. PR-6 leaves government fieldless, so neither the schema default nor this row may branch on a field. A branch root that recommends what its schema already recommends is the schema's default template under a second name. (3) PRIVACY RULES — identical. Both carry `potentially_sensitive` for the same reason: authority holdings mix published instruments with casework, submissions, and restricted data. This row proposes no stricter and no looser posture. Contrast the siblings that DO earn their rows on this leg: `government.legislative-record` treats recorded votes and verbatim proceedings as published by design while treating inquiry submissions and pre-introduction drafting as stricter than the default, and `government.constituent-casework` adds cross-person suppression around an intermediary's authority-to-act. This row adds nothing of the kind. Separately, it is a residual wearing a domain's clothes. Its job description is already written and already owned by P10/P11: "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group." Building it would reinstate the failure mode the roster work exists to end — an industry label whose only content is a name and a one-liner. Refusing costs no coverage and no protection: activation, safety posture, universal facts, and grouping all attach through the `government` schema, which is unaffected.

deterministic: None of its own. This is the finding, not an omission. After subtracting the thirty named government siblings, every remaining authority-side signal is one the `government` schema anchor already carries in its own deterministic list, and the schema fires on it directly. Everything recorded here exists so a later reader can check the refusal rather than take it on trust.

The residue that is genuinely NOT covered by a sibling is a public body's internal corporate paperwork — its device register, staff rota, facilities log, internal budget, purchase card statement. Those are business_operations shapes whose only claim to this schema is owner type. `business_operations.it-asset-inventory` reached the same conclusion from its side and left the edge unauthored, recording that "the confusion is about the *owner type*, which the schema anchor already handles at family level".
needs_llm: Nothing is routed here. An officially-shaped file that matches no sibling situation is the ordinary ambiguous case: it goes to the bounded model step against the `government` SCHEMA, and to a residual home if nothing lands. The design's abstention rule governs, not a catch-all row.
never_alone: a government department, regulator, municipality, legislature, court, public school, archive, or museum name, or an official-looking seal, alone — the whole of this row's residual candidate evidence, and the reason it cannot exist. The body may be issuer, counterparty, subject, employer, cited authority, research venue, or service provider, and the roster hint's own phrase 'issued by, or addressed to' collapses two opposite custody roles into one row.

'issued by OR addressed to a public body' offered as a two-role relation. It is not one. 'Addressed to' is the recipient's custody, which the schema anchor already excludes: "an authority-issued permit, licence, tax notice, benefit letter, identity card, visa, voting confirmation, filing acknowledgement, or registry extract held by the recipient" is never-alone for this schema. A disjunction of a role and its opposite resolves nothing about which side the holder is on, and holder side is the only thing the whole `government` family turns on.

'no more specific sub-domain applies'. An absence is not a signal, cannot be extracted as evidence, and cannot be checked against a file. It is a routing rule about the sibling set, and routing rules of exactly that shape are what the residual library is.
a .gov-style domain, government email address, coat of arms, letterhead, footer, PDF producer string, or metadata author alone.
a parent folder named Government, Council, Public, Regulatory, Civic, or Policy alone.
a shared download session of official PDFs; "A session should never be treated as proof of topic".
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to "treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning".

template.why: Empty because the row is refused, and empty in any case by binding contract: the government schema declares no field rows under PR-6, so no destination-eligible field exists to order. The absence of a distinguishing dimension order is itself part of the refusal — the schema anchor already records the only recommendation there is, that authority-side function or bounded proceeding comes before an exact reference and then work type, that named people must not become the organizing dimension, and that time is not first because "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." This row would restate that sentence and change nothing in it.

falls_through_to.why: The home this refused row was really describing, already written and already owned by P10/P11: "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group." A standalone public notice, permit, licence, published decision or civic confirmation with durable value and no authority-side workflow lands here.

The correct home when an unattached official document carries a named individual's casework, identity, benefit, immigration, complaint or election data. "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts." Refusing the row costs nothing in protection, because this posture attaches through P7 and the schema, not through a branch root.

The home for a law, judgment, statutory guidance, official-statistics release, consultation paper or government report held for reading rather than as authority-side work. "Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association."

The cautious outcome for a document that looks official or administrative but whose holder role, public-body status, or operational purpose cannot be settled safely — including the public body's internal corporate paperwork whose only government evidence is owner type. "Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision."

The safe outcome for an encrypted archive, case-system backup, damaged export or unknown binary that cannot yield evidence beyond metadata. "Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats."

sensitivity_why: Recorded even though the row is refused, so the refusal cannot be read as weakening protection for the files it would have caught. Authority-adjacent documents routinely carry named individuals — casework, complaints, benefits, immigration, submissions, evaluator declarations, election operations — and the design's operative limit governs regardless of which template holds them: "Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it." That limit attaches through P7 and the `government` schema, which already carries this same value and reasoning; that identity is itself the third leg of the refusal. This entry assigns only the catalogue value `potentially_sensitive` and assigns, aliases, ranks, and infers no handling class.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH (two items). (1) Nine landed rows author a `collides_with` edge naming this id — `government.legislative-record`, `government.elections-administration`, `government.emergency-management`, `government.constituent-casework`, `government.archives-recordkeeping`, `government.diplomatic-consular`, `business_operations.board-governance`, `business_operations.corporate-regulatory-filings`, `construction_property.site-health-safety` — and several use 'the generic authority-side default' and this id interchangeably in the same sentence, which is the refusal's own best evidence. This row does not edit them. R1c must decide whether each edge is re-pointed at the `government` schema (recommended: the boundary argued is a schema-level holder-side boundary in every case) or whether the id is retained as an alias target. (2) One real pile may have been thrown away with the branch root: a public body's own constitutional and governance instruments — constitution, standing orders, scheme of delegation, members' register of interests, code of conduct, statement of accounts — which `government.municipal-administration` holds for a council but no row holds for a non-municipal agency, regulator or trust. If that is what the branch root was for, the honest fix is a NEW narrow row named for that situation, not the reinstatement of a catch-all. This row does not create one, because minting a replacement id is outside what a single node agent may do.
